why: The Masoretic setumah after חַטּוּשׁ puts 'of the sons of Shecaniah' with v.3 (Zechariah), while 1 Esdras reads Hattush son of Shecaniah, so the verse division leaves it undecided.
Ezra 7:1-3 telescopes the 1CH 6 high-priest line, so this Azariah (father of Amariah) is the Azariah of 1CH 6:10-11 already on the row; azariah-24 would only duplicate him.
1CH 1:17 compresses Aram's sons into 'sons of Shem' (Gether is Aram's son, GEN 10:23), and 'gether descendant-of shem' is already recorded.
וְאֶחָיו in Neh 12:36 means Zechariah's fellow Levite musicians or kinsmen, not his siblings, so no brother relation is stated.
וְאֶחָיו in Neh 12:36 means Zechariah's fellow Levite musicians or kinsmen, not his siblings, so no brother relation is stated.
ואחיתיהם in 1CH 2:16 makes Zeruiah the sister of the sons of Jesse just listed, Ozem among them, and nothing between them is recorded.
ואחיתיהם in 1CH 2:16 makes Abigail the sister of Jesse's sons, Raddai among them, and abigail-2 is that Abigail (sister of Zeruiah).
The Masoretic text of Ezra 8:10 names no Bani (only 'of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah'); Bani comes from an LXX/1 Esdras restoration, so the chapter does not say it.
1CH 3:9 calls Tamar 'their sister' (אֲחוֹתָם) of all David's sons listed, which include Chileab (named Daniel in 3:1); the site already uses sister-of for half-siblings (Amnon).
GEN 25:4's כָּל־אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי קְטוּרָה covers Jokshan's son Sheba (25:3), so he is Keturah's grandson, and nothing between them is recorded.
1CH 4:1 is a descending line (Perez, Hezron, ...), and Hezron is Perez's son (GEN 46:12, already recorded), so 'son-of judah' is false.
The Eliel son of Toah in 1CH 6:34 is Samuel's ancestor, Elihu son of Tohu (1SA 1:1), not the Manassite head, so the row belongs on elihu.
'Sons of Beriah' closes the list only at 1CH 8:16, and whether it reaches back to 8:14 (Jeremoth) or covers only Michael, Ispah and Joha is not settled by the text.
The Eleazar son of Phinehas weighing silver in Ezra's day cannot be the son of Aaron's grandson Phinehas, so phinehas-3 is the right father.
In צִדְקִיָּה בְנוֹ, 'his son' can refer to Jehoiakim or to Jeconiah, and 1CH 3:16 does not resolve which.
In Neh 12:15, Meraioth is a priestly house whose head was Helkai, not the Meraioth son of Ahitub (meraioth-2), and no descent is stated.
In 1CH 5:13-14, the seven brethren (Sheba among them) are introduced with אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי אֲבִיחַיִל, so Sheba is a son of Abihail.
Zia and Eber are listed together among the seven sons of Abihail (1CH 5:13-14), which makes them brothers, and this is not recorded.
1CH 3:19-20 continues the list of Zerubbabel's children with the further five ('Hashubah ... Jushab-hesed, five') before Hananiah's sons begin in 3:21, so Berechiah is Zerubbabel's son.
In 1CH 7:16, וּבָנָיו ('his sons') can refer to Peresh, the main subject, or to Sheresh, the nearest name, so the father of Ulam is not decided.
Ezra 8:13 names יְעִיאֵל among 'the last sons of Adonikam', so the chapter does say it.

The setumah puts 'of the sons of Shecaniah' apart from Zechariah, whom the verse makes 'of the sons of Parosh', and shecaniah-2 is the priestly-course head of 1CH 24:11 in any case, so the row is unsupported.
The Masoretic text reads אֲבִי עֵיטָם ('the father of Etam', likely a place founder) rather than 'sons of Etam' (LXX), so Jezreel's sonship to an Etam is not decided.
Mizzah is Reuel's son and Reuel is Basemath's son (GEN 36:4), so בְּנֵי בָשְׂמַת in 36:13 means grandson.
1CH 7:13 calls Naphtali's sons, Jahziel among them, בְּנֵי בִלְהָה, and he is her grandson; nothing directly between them is recorded.
Neh 11:15 does say 'Hashabiah son of Bunni'; the trouble is that hashabiah-2 is Jeduthun's son, which calls for a repoint, not a removal.
In 1CH 3:17, אַסִּר may be a son's name or mean 'the captive' describing Jeconiah, and the text does not decide which.
Ezra 8's clans repeat the Ezra 2 list, so 'sons of Shephatiah' is the clan of Ezra 2:4 (shephatiah-5), and shephatiah-10 would duplicate it.
Ezra 7:1's 'Seraiah son of Azariah son of Hilkiah' is the chief priest of 1CH 6:13-14 and 2KI 25:18 (seraiah-2), and seraiah-11 would duplicate him.
Neh 12:36 lists Maai and Gilalai as Zechariah's אַחִים (fellow musicians), and nothing makes them siblings of each other.
1CH 5:14 does say בֶּן־מִיכָאֵל בֶּן־יְשִׁישַׁי; the record's conflation with the 5:13 Michael is a separate problem, not grounds for removing the row.
1CH 4:19 makes Eshtemoa a brother of the unnamed 'father of Keilah', not of Keilah (likely a town), so 'brother of Keilah' is not stated.
The reach of 'sons of Beriah' (8:16) back to 8:14 is undecided, and וְאַחְיוֹ is often read as 'and his brothers' rather than a name.
Hul is Aram's son (GEN 10:23), 1CH 1:17 compresses the generations, and 'hul descendant-of shem' is already recorded.
In 1CH 5:13-14, the seven, Eber (Heber) among them, are אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי אֲבִיחַיִל.
Ezra 8:8 plainly puts Zebadiah 'of the sons of Shephatiah', the clan of Ezra 2:4, so the row is supported.
Zerah is Reuel's son and Basemath's grandson (GEN 36:4, 13), so 'son-of' is the wrong type; it should be grandson-of.
ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ says only that Rahab bore Boaz to Salmon (the same formula is used of Tamar and Judah), so MAT 1:5 does not state a marriage.
In 1CH 5:13-14, the seven, Jacan (Jachan) among them, are אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי אֲבִיחַיִל.
Shammah is Reuel's son and Basemath's grandson (GEN 36:4, 13), so 'son-of' is the wrong type.
Uz is Aram's son (GEN 10:23, already recorded), and 1CH 1:17 compresses the generations, so 'son-of shem' is false (descendant-of would be the correct type).
In 1CH 4:19, אֲבִי קְעִילָה can stand in apposition to Naham or name the first of the wife's sons, and the text does not decide which.
1CH 3:19-20 continues Zerubbabel's children with the five ending in Jushab-hesed before Hananiah's line begins, so he is Zerubbabel's son.
Ard is Bela's son (NUM 26:40), and GEN 46:21's wider 'sons of Benjamin' is already recorded as 'ard descendant-of benjamin'.
MAT 1:5 says only that Salmon fathered Boaz ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ, which does not state that Rahab was his wife.
Ezra 8:13 names Jeiel among 'the last sons of Adonikam', so the chapter does say it.
Hashubah heads the further five children of Zerubbabel in 1CH 3:20, after Meshullam, Hananiah and Shelomith.
GEN 46:17 makes Malchiel a son of Beriah, Asher's son, so grandson-of the person Asher is exact.
1CH 7:39 says Arah is a son of Ulla, and nothing in the text identifies Ulla with Jephunneh.
1CH 7:13 calls Naphtali's sons, Jahziel among them, בְּנֵי בִלְהָה, and he is her grandson; nothing directly between them is recorded.
